description: Hand-labeled Perl verdict corpus: one-line rewrites in three small authored Perl distributions (Test::More, Test2::V0 and Test::Exception), each with the fact packet the pinned perl-ripr-facts producer wrote for that diff, labeled with what the distribution's own tests actually discriminate, so ripr's Perl verdicts can be scored as false actionable, false exposed, false silent, abstained, or ideal. A second group of cases edits a producer packet to carry a RIPR-SPEC-0235 fact the producer cannot emit yet.
label_method: For each case the rewrite was applied to a fresh copy of the authored distribution and `prove -l t` was run to confirm it keeps every test green (behavior_preserving_rewrite). Each listed mutant of the rewritten text was then applied by hand on the anchor line and `prove -l t` run again; no Perl mutation tool drives Test::More, Test2 and Test::Exception alike, so the mutants are hand-written and each was reviewed for equivalence. A mutant counts as detected (`tests_failed`) when prove fails after every file compiles, and its failing_test names the test file and the failing assertion's name. Truth is derived from the count of mutants with tests_failed: all is discriminated, none is not_discriminated, otherwise partially_discriminated. The fact packet comes from `fact_producer` run on the same diff; an edited_producer packet names its edits and has its fingerprint recomputed.
verdict_projection: Only candidate_current findings on the anchor file and line count. For Perl, a finding whose source_currentness is unresolved_subject also counts, because every Perl finding carries that currentness today (#3280): ripr reads a packet, not the source, so it never resolves the subject itself. exposed is credited; a named static_limit_kind or a no_static_path, infection_unknown, propagation_unknown or static_unknown class is limited; any other class (weakly_exposed, reachable_unrevealed) is a gap. A gap on the line outranks credit, and credit outranks a limit. No anchored finding is silent. Rates are also reported by packet provenance, so producer packets and edited packets never mix.
non_claims: Rates describe this corpus only; they are not a population estimate for Perl code or for ripr in general.
Every subject is authored to fill a cell of ripr's Perl oracle and reach rules; its rates are not real-world rates.
ripr does not parse Perl. Every verdict here is ripr's reading of a committed fact packet, so a wrong verdict can come from the producer's facts or from ripr's rules; the case reasoning says which.
edited_producer cases measure ripr's rules on facts the pinned producer does not emit; they are not evidence about the producer.
Truth comes from the listed hand-written mutants, not from exhaustive mutation; a discriminated label means every listed mutant made prove fail.
The harness does not run Perl, prove, the fact producer, mutation testing, or any network access.

fact_producer.name: perl-ripr-facts
fact_producer.command: perl-ripr-facts ripr-facts --root <subject> --base base --head HEAD --diff <case>.diff --out <case>.json, run from the subject's parent directory with the subject committed as `base` and the rewrite as HEAD

cases.hard_case: The test calls discount() imported through Exporter; the producer proves direct_owner_call only for a package-qualified call, so the only relation is file_proximity to the package.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 100 no longer earns the discount
not equivalent: 100 no longer earns the discount

mutants.failing_test: t/pricing.t: no discount just below the threshold
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 99 earns the discount

cases.reasoning: is(discount(100), 90) and is(discount(99), 99) sit on both sides of the threshold, so any move of the boundary fails a test. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 (relation kinds), Test::More is().

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a 20 kg parcel pays 15
not equivalent: a 25 kg parcel pays 5

cases.reasoning: ok(shipping_fee(25)) only checks that the fee is truthy; both fees (5 and 15) pass, so no boundary mutant fails. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 smoke_ok/weak_smoke.

cases.hard_case: The exact is() targets the changed sub but its inputs (2000, 10) sit far from the 1000 threshold; the producer still records the changed predicate as the oracle's observed_sink.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 1000 points become silver
not equivalent: 1200 points become silver

cases.reasoning: Inputs 2000 and 10 are far from 1000, so moving the gold threshold changes no asserted value. An exact assertion on the owner is not observation of the changed predicate. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 sink alignment, #5498.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 100 spent earns 20 points
not equivalent: 100 spent earns 1000 points

cases.reasoning: cmp_ok(loyalty_points(100), '>', 0) accepts any positive count, so changing the divisor or operator keeps it green. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 predicate_boundary_assertion (cmp_ok).

cases.hard_case: is_deeply compares the whole returned hash across several lines; the producer leaves observed_sink empty for the hash-field change, so ripr reads the strong exact oracle as observation_unconfirmed.

mutants.failing_test: t/qualified.t: quote adds shipping to the discounted subtotal
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: total becomes -85

mutants.failing_test: t/qualified.t: quote adds shipping to the discounted subtotal
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: shipping is dropped from the total

cases.reasoning: is_deeply pins subtotal, shipping and total, so any change to how total is computed fails the test. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 hash_or_object_field, #5498 observation_unconfirmed.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 2 rounds to 3.00
not equivalent: 2 rounds to -2.00
not equivalent: three decimals

cases.reasoning: like() checks only the two-decimal shape: a mutant that shifts the value keeps the shape and passes, while sign or precision mutants fail. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 like/weak_broad.

cases.hard_case: isnt() rejects exactly one value; the producer maps it to a strong exact oracle and records the changed predicate as its observed sink.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: an order of 100 is no longer clamped
not equivalent: 110 is no longer clamped
not equivalent: clamped orders become 98

cases.reasoning: isnt(clamp_qty(150), 150) only rejects 150, so moving the clamp threshold or the clamp value keeps it green. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 oracle strength (isnt).

cases.hard_case: Assertions sit inside a subtest and call the sub through an Exporter import, so the producer relates the test to the package only.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 50 is not bulk
not equivalent: 49 is bulk

cases.reasoning: is_bulk(50) and is_bulk(49) bracket the threshold inside a subtest, so either boundary mutant fails. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 subtest test facts.

cases.hard_case: Table-driven: the assertion runs inside a for loop over a data table, and the call is an Exporter import.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: south pays 20%
not equivalent: north pays 25%

cases.reasoning: Both regions are asserted with exact expected tax, so changing either rate fails one row of the table. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 relation kinds.

cases.hard_case: The is() lives in a test-file helper sub that receives the expected value as an argument.

mutants.failing_test: t/bulk.t: three items earn the bundle discount
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: three items lose the discount
not equivalent: two items earn the discount

cases.reasoning: check_bundle() asserts both three items (discount) and two items (none), so moving the threshold either way fails. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 helper_call (deferred).

cases.hard_case: The test reaches the changed code through an instance method call; the producer does not prove method receivers.

mutants.failing_test: t/cart.t: total multiplies price by quantity
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: total becomes 18

mutants.failing_test: t/cart.t: total multiplies price by quantity
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: quantity is ignored

cases.reasoning: is($cart->total, 25) pins price times quantity over two lines, so either mutant fails. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 method_receiver.

cases.hard_case: The test reaches item_count only through $self->$action() with the method name as data, a dynamic dispatch no static relation can follow.

mutants.failing_test: t/cart.t: run dispatches to the named action
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: two items count as three

mutants.failing_test: t/cart.t: run dispatches to the named action
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: two items count as one

cases.reasoning: is($cart->run('item_count'), 2) fails for any change to the count. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 dynamic boundaries.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: two amounts count as three
not equivalent: total doubles

cases.reasoning: Test2's is() compares the whole hash deeply, so changing count or total fails it. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 Test2::V0 is().

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the sign is dropped
not equivalent: the sign flips

cases.reasoning: like(..., qr/^2026/) only checks the date prefix, so dropping or flipping the sign keeps it green. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 Test2 like/weak_broad.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: zero reads as overdrawn
not equivalent: -1 is no longer overdrawn

cases.reasoning: ok(is_overdrawn(-1)) passes when zero becomes overdrawn but fails when -1 stops being overdrawn: one of two mutants is caught. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 smoke_ok.

cases.hard_case: The exception is observed through like(dies { ... }, qr/.../), which the producer maps to a weak broad exception observer.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the message no longer says funds
not equivalent: overdrawing by 10 no longer dies

cases.reasoning: The regex pins 'insufficient funds' and the call overdraws by 10, so changing the message or raising the threshold fails. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 exception_observer.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the deposit subtracts the balance
not equivalent: the deposit is ignored

cases.reasoning: ok(lives { deposit(5, 5) }) checks only that deposit does not die; its return value is never asserted. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 lives/weak_smoke.

cases.hard_case: isnt() rejects one value; the producer maps it to a strong exact oracle and records the changed line as its observed sink.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the fee doubles
not equivalent: the fee drops tenfold

cases.reasoning: isnt(fee(100), 0) only rejects zero, so a doubled or tenfold-smaller fee keeps it green. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 oracle strength (isnt).

cases.hard_case: The call is an Exporter import, so the producer relates the test to the package only.

mutants.failing_test: t/ledger.t: net change sums signed amounts
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 5 and -3 net to -2

mutants.failing_test: t/ledger.t: net change sums signed amounts
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 5 and -3 net to 8

cases.reasoning: is(net_change(5, -3), 2) fails when the sum subtracts or takes absolute values. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 relation kinds.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a zero month is short
not equivalent: a month short by one is balanced

cases.reasoning: The subtest asserts a zero month (balanced) and a month short by one (short), so either boundary mutant fails. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 Test2 subtest.

cases.hard_case: throws_ok with a message regex pins the exception text, but the producer maps every throws_ok to a weak broad exception observer.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the message no longer says funds
not equivalent: overdrawing 20 from 10 no longer dies

cases.reasoning: throws_ok { withdraw(10, 20) } qr/insufficient funds/ fails if the message changes or the overdraw stops dying. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 Test::Exception throws_ok.

cases.hard_case: The boundary is pinned by a pair: throws_ok one over the balance and lives_ok at the balance. Neither oracle alone is exact.

mutants.failing_test: t/account.t: the whole balance may move
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: moving the whole balance dies

mutants.failing_test: t/account.t: one over the balance dies
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: one over the balance is allowed

cases.reasoning: Moving the comparison either way breaks one side of the pair. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 throws_ok, lives_ok.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 100 cannot close
not equivalent: 200 can close

cases.reasoning: dies_ok { close_out(1000) } only checks a balance far above 100, so moving the threshold keeps it green. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 dies_ok.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: interest doubles
not equivalent: interest is 400 times larger

cases.reasoning: lives_ok { interest(100) } never looks at the returned interest. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 lives_ok/weak_smoke.

cases.hard_case: throws_ok with a class name pins the exception class, which the producer maps to a weak broad exception observer.

mutants.failing_test: t/account.t: freezing raises an account error
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a plain string is not an Account::Error

mutants.failing_test: t/account.t: freezing raises an account error
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: a reason no longer freezes

cases.reasoning: throws_ok { freeze('fraud') } 'Account::Error' fails for a plain string die and for a freeze that no longer dies. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 Test::Exception throws_ok class.

mutants.failing_test: t/account.t: a withdrawal costs a fee of one
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the fee doubles

mutants.failing_test: t/account.t: a withdrawal costs a fee of one
mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the fee becomes a refund

cases.reasoning: lives_and { is(balance_after(10, 4), 5) } pins the fee of one, so either fee mutant fails. Spec cells: RIPR-SPEC-0064 lives_and.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: wrapping costs 4 per item
not equivalent: two items cost 5

cases.reasoning: t/load.t only loads Shop::Pricing and checks can_ok for gift_wrap_fee; no test calls it, so both mutants survive. ripr reports no_static_path, a limit rather than the ideal gap, because a mention-only oracle gives no relation to the change.

cases.hard_case: RIPR-SPEC-0235 example 1: the strong oracle carries no observed_sink, so the packet cannot confirm the assertion reaches the changed return.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: two amounts count as three
not equivalent: total doubles

cases.reasoning: is(summary(...), {total=>..., count=>...}) pins both fields, so both mutants fail t/ledger.t. With the observed sink removed the spec asks for withheld credit with an unconfirmed-observation reason, not a repairable weakness; a weakly_exposed verdict here is a false actionable.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: two amounts count as three
not equivalent: total doubles

cases.reasoning: The test discriminates both mutants, but the packet says reachability is unknown, so the spec's answer is static_unknown, a limit. ripr follows the hint.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: two amounts count as three
not equivalent: total doubles

cases.reasoning: Both mutants fail t/ledger.t. The spec treats a sink that matches after whitespace normalization as aligned, so ideal is exposed; weakly_exposed is a false actionable.

cases.hard_case: RIPR-SPEC-0235 example 23: a missing_test_runner dynamic boundary on the test file.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: two amounts count as three
not equivalent: total doubles

cases.reasoning: Both mutants fail t/ledger.t when prove runs it. The spec says a missing runner boundary should withhold credit (a limit); ripr ignores the boundary and reports exposed, which this corpus scores as credited because the test does discriminate. The case keeps the boundary visible for a later spec-conformance check.

cases.hard_case: RIPR-SPEC-0235 example 28: the relation names a different test file than the oracle that carries the sink.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: 1000 points become silver

cases.reasoning: The only assertion on tier_label checks 1200 and 50 points, far from 1000, so both boundary mutants survive. The spec says an oracle from another test cannot credit the relation (reachable_unrevealed); ripr still reports exposed, a false exposed.
